name: Alfa Romeo T33/2
description:
The Alfa Romeo Tipo 33/2, affectionately nicknamed "Daytona" after its stunning debut, represents Autodelta's refined approach to the 2-liter prototype class. After a challenging 1967 season with the original T33, legendary engineer Carlo Chiti went back to the drawing board to create a more competitive machine.

While retaining the tubular "H" chassis from the first-generation T33, Chiti's team lowered the front end and redesigned the rear bodywork to improve handling characteristics. The all-aluminum 2.0-liter V8 was slightly enlarged to 1,998cc, now producing 270 horsepower - more than enough to outpace their rivals from Porsche in the 2-liter class. The engine's remarkable ability to rev to over 10,000 RPM made it a thrilling powerplant to exploit.

The T33/2 made its debut at the 1968 24 Hours of Daytona, where it dominated the 2-liter Prototype class and finished 5th, 6th, and 7th overall - a remarkable achievement that earned the short-tail variant its famous nickname. Success continued at Mugello, Imola, and Zandvoort, with the Belgian privateer team VDS proving particularly effective with their two T33/2s.

A long-tail variant was developed for Le Mans, winning the 2-liter class at the 1968 race, while factory Autodelta teams claimed the same honors at the Targa Florio on home soil. Approximately 28 cars were built, enabling Group 4 homologation for 1969. The T33/2's success laid the groundwork for the even more potent T33/3, as Australian team owner Alec Mildren's development of a 2.5-liter V8 variant proved to Chiti that a 3.0-liter evolution was possible.
author: Team WSC Legends
